chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn Asbat, on the authority of Ali ibn Salim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, who said: Ali ibn al-Hussein (peace be upon them) said:

May God have mercy upon al-Abbas, meaning ibn Ali, who preferred his father and sacrificed his brother with his own self, until his two hands were cut off. God granted him in place of them two wings with which he flies with the angels in Paradise, just as He did for Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. And indeed, for al-Abbas with God, the Blessed and Exalted, is a rank with which all the martyrs envy him on the Day of Resurrection. The hadith is long; we have taken from it what is needed, and I have presented it in its entirety along with what I narrated regarding the virtues of al-Abbas ibn Ali (peace be upon them) in the book Maqtal al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الْعَبَّاس: Al-Abbas, referring to Abbas ibn Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward and rank of Abbas ibn Ali in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) to establish the unique spiritual rank of Abbas ibn Ali, emphasizing that his physical sacrifice—specifically the severing of his hands—was divinely transformed into literal wings for flight among the angels. This comparison to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib underscores a shared status of martyrdom and divine favor, while the note that all martyrs will envy his position highlights a distinct superiority in the hereafter, a theme frequently explored in Shia hagiography regarding the Ahl al-Bayt's companions.
